motion.name: skill-inversion
motion.purpose: Reveal home skill inversion from left to right on fine-pointer hover or keyboard focus. Applied only with no reduced-motion preference.

motion.name: button-tone
motion.purpose: Filled and outlined button tone changes. Applied only with no reduced-motion preference.

motion.name: evidence-location
motion.purpose: Evidence location scrolls smoothly unless reduced motion is requested; question switching focuses and reveals the new prompt with automatic scrolling.

motion.name: listening-option-tone
motion.purpose: Listening choice hover and selection tone changes only without reduced motion.

motion.name: listening-columns
motion.value: 30fps maximum; scaleY(.035) rest; transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1) on inactive columns
motion.purpose: 48 columns use actual 0–8kHz analyser data. Direct transforms stop when paused, compact, removed, reduced-motion, offscreen or hidden; no synthetic motion.

motion.name: listening-transcript
motion.value: transform/opacity 240ms entrance, 180ms exit; cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1) transform easing
motion.purpose: Native nonmodal popover enters from the right. Keyboard opening and reduced-motion changes are immediate; native dismissal and focus restoration remain available.

motion.name: speaking-entry-tone
motion.purpose: Equal Speaking overview entries invert on hover or keyboard focus. Applied only without reduced motion.

motion.name: navigation-key
motion.purpose: Pointer route selection wipes the white navigation key from left to right, with inverted labels and a focus ring above the key. Keyboard and reduced-motion changes are immediate.

motion.name: button-press
motion.purpose: Shared Piano buttons acknowledge a pointer press. Position stays unchanged for keyboard activation and reduced motion; existing button tone remains.

motion.name: mobile-navigation
motion.value: transform 220ms cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1); opacity 160ms ease; discrete display exit
motion.purpose: The mobile rail and backdrop enter/exit without delaying interaction or focus. Closed surfaces are inert immediately. Keyboard/reduced-motion changes and unsupported browsers use immediate fallback.

narrative.overview:
A quiet local learning workspace, organized through the relationship between black piano keys and white paper. Simple lines, square controls, and restrained interface type make choosing a skill, reading, answering, and understanding evidence feel like one continuous activity. The five skills retain equal standing; the interface does not prescribe a learning order.

This record describes the implemented common Web/Electron learning shell, home, reading workspace, listening workspace, four Speaking routes (overview, AI coach, sentence pronunciation and article read-aloud), the standalone Vocabulary and Writing workspaces, and the Records and Settings utility pages including model configuration. Listening extends the same piano world through a continuous answer sheet, a compact sticky player, sound columns, and a nonmodal transcript. Speaking extends it through a continuous notebook, inline pronunciation evidence and a reserved recording dock. Vocabulary extends it through parallel recall and reference, equal memory ratings and optional pronunciation. Writing extends it through an immutable original linked to a correction margin, a separate draft and complete review evidence. Records and Settings extend it through ruled history rows, native filters, section links and grouped forms using the existing controls. The contextual vocabulary collector in Listening and Speaking retains its own existing flow. The Windows native titlebar remains intact; unused drag-strip and window-strip CSS does not establish a custom titlebar behavior.
keyCharacteristics: True white learning surfaces with a black sidebar and white current item.
Thin neutral rules and square, plainly labeled controls.
Five equal home entries with a temporary sweeping inversion.
Readable article prose beside questions and answer evidence.
A continuous listening sheet with real-audio columns and an explicitly opened transcript.
A continuous speaking notebook with evidence owned by each turn or paragraph.
Parallel word recall and reference, with pronunciation separate from memory ratings.
Visible keyboard focus, responsive stacking, and reduced-motion support.
Ruled completed-practice keys connect a saved Reading or Listening result to the original answer evidence.

rules.name: The Neutral Canvas Rule
rules.body: The piano learning canvas stays true white. Color is not added to imply skill priority or to replace an answer's written result and evidence.

rules.name: The Reading Measure Rule
rules.body: Preserve the article's generous line height and readable measure when extending the reader; compact metadata must not determine prose density.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Retain line and tone as the means of separation for piano surfaces; do not inherit decorative shadows from older module pages.

rules.name: The Equal Keys Rule
rules.body: No skill is pre-inverted or permanently promoted. Fine-pointer hover and keyboard focus reveal a left-to-right inversion over (220ms), using `cubic-bezier(.4, 0, .2, 1)`. Touch has no sticky hover treatment. With reduced motion, the same state change is immediate.

rules.name: The Sound Follows Audio Rule
rules.body: Columns respond only to actual audio data; silence and pause do not generate decorative motion. Playback never waits for the visualization. A failed graph or resume operation disables the visual; when the media element has already been captured by Web Audio, a fresh ordinary media element restores its position and speed and resumes playback.

dos: Do build new piano surfaces from true white, black, and neutral rules with square controls.
Do preserve equal resting emphasis for all five home skill entries.
Do keep article prose spacious and make answer evidence easy to locate and return from.
Do provide visible keyboard focus, meaningful labels, and immediate state changes for reduced motion.
Do keep interface language independent from AI explanation language and learning content.
Do treat the existing shell, home, reader, listening workspace, four Speaking routes, Vocabulary and Writing workspaces, Records and Settings as the implemented reference when extending this system.
Do keep listening playback controls available when columns stop or the audio graph fails.
Do preserve Speaking's original phone evidence, separate metrics, pending states and previous successful results alongside written feedback.
donts: Don't promote the older green/cream palette, decorative fonts, rounded cards, or shadows into piano tokens.
Don't turn the home entries into a prioritized card grid or keep one entry inverted at rest.
Don't replace written feedback and quoted evidence with color alone.
Don't add custom desktop window controls or treat unused drag-strip CSS as implemented behavior.
Don't turn Speaking's semantic verdict colors or legacy assessment fallback styles into global decorative tokens.
